channel.description: Recent content on My New Hugo Project

item.title: Cascaded Shadow Maps Without the Shimmer
item.description: A single shadow map can’t cover a large outdoor scene at a useful resolution. Cascaded shadow maps split the view frustum into slices, each with its own map.

item.title: SIMD by Hand: Vectorizing a Dot Product
item.description: The compiler auto-vectorizes a lot, but not everything. Writing one kernel by hand is the fastest way to learn what it can and can’t do for you.

item.title: Designing a Compact G-Buffer for Deferred Shading
item.description: Deferred shading trades memory bandwidth for flexible lighting. The G-buffer is where that bandwidth goes, so every byte per pixel counts.

item.title: False Sharing: When Your Threads Fight Over a Cache Line
item.description: Two threads, two counters, zero shared state — and yet the program runs slower than the single-threaded version. The culprit is almost always false sharing.

item.title: Branchless Code and the Branch Predictor
item.description: A mispredicted branch costs roughly 15–20 cycles on a modern core. On unpredictable data that adds up quickly, which is why “branchless” tricks exist.

item.title: GPU-Driven Frustum Culling with Compute Shaders
item.description: Once a scene has tens of thousands of objects, CPU culling and draw submission become the bottleneck. Moving both to the GPU removes that bottleneck.
